knowledgeAnswers.rationale: The buyer fixes the result and the measures and leaves the method open, which is the output or performance style. A conformance style would fix the design, and a brand-name style would fix the product, so both remove the supplier's room to propose a design.

A single named brand tells suppliers that equal alternatives will not be considered, even if one would meet the performance measures. Naming a brand does not make the supplier responsible for the design, and it does not guarantee a low price.

Early discussion with potential suppliers and with users tests assumptions about what the market offers and what the work involves. Past invoices show only what was bought before, and a competitor's confidential response must never be used.

Features that add nothing to the outcome are paid for in the price. Over-specification tends to narrow competition and can increase disputes or maintenance effort, so the other two options describe the opposite effects.

practicalCriteria: Learner writes one requirement for a real or invented purchase and states the specification style with a one-line reason that names who carries the design risk. Pass: the reason is present and is consistent with the style chosen.

Learner's draft contains no unexplained brand name. Pass: any brand that remains is followed by an equivalent clause and at least one performance criterion, or has a recorded reason for a single brand.
Learner's requirements are testable. Pass: every requirement states a measure, a test or an observable result, and the assessor can tick each one without needing the learner to explain it.
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks. A quiz pass is not verified practical competence; the assessor signs off the practical criteria separately.
evidenceRequired: Completed specification draft saved with a version date and owner
Record of at least one user and one potential supplier consulted, with the change made
Assessor record of knowledge check result
Assessor sign-off against the three practical criteria
stopWorkCriteria: Learner treats the three specification styles as official definitions, when they are general concepts
Learner uses confidential information from one organisation to shape a request sent to another
Learner treats the Commonwealth Procurement Rules as binding on a private business without checking the scope of paragraphs 3.7 to 3.10
